Thx @tkstanczak also! **EIP 1559 Implementers' Call #4** **Date**: Wednesday Aug 28th at 15:00 UTC **Agenda**: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/197 **Zoom**: www.zoom.us/j/91866526216 It won't be livestreamed, but I'll upload the zoom recording afterwards. Please add anything you'd like to discuss to the agenda 😄 Hey everyone, I could really use some help. I'm trying to write a script to verify the total supply of ETH. I'm stuck on the genesis block currently. I know that the initial distribution of ETH is hard-coded somewhere, but I can't seem to find it in the (geth) codebase. The best I've found so far is in this repo: https://github.com/ethereum/pyethsaletool/blob/cab1c9d8ca27f5e86a9eb36a2a56915f5f7830d1/genesis_block.json That seems to give the correct information for the inintial sale, minus the supply given to the foundation I really would like to know where this information is stored in geth, and if you have any information about the other clients I would love to know that as well. I really want to be able to trust this initial genesis state, and show to others that it can be trusted. Thanks! You can probably take a look at Etherscan too: https://etherscan.io/block/0 if you want specifically geth, then you want this: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blame/48b484c5ac537d1759c9903ce81302c298f03a84/core/genesis_alloc.go#L24 (github can't render it) to get a list of transactions out of there, you can use this function https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/master/core/genesis.go#L420 that is where geth creates it: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/master/core/genesis.go#L342 Perfect! Thank you <tkstanczak> <@443823988561412097> this is where Nethermind has it: https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/master/src/Nethermind/Chains/foundation.json <tkstanczak> just allocations from this file <tkstanczak> then you need each block body <tkstanczak> and the block numbers at which the rewards changed <tkstanczak> the rewatd changes are defined in the chainspec file too <tkstanczak> you need block bodies because you need to know the exact number of uncles for each block <tkstanczak> the more uncles the morw emission Perfect, thanks! I really appreciate it. Do you know where the official documentation is for the reward based on uncles? <tkstanczak> https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/blob/master/src/Nethermind/Nethermind.Blockchain/Rewards/RewardCalculator.cs <tkstanczak> 20 lines of code, better than documentation ICYMI, it seems like most block explorers are *not* reporting the same supply (https://twitter.com/factcheckmypost/status/1291863378793828359, https://twitter.com/zackvoell/status/1291876817327005698). This is embarrassing IMO and I wonder if we should try and get clients to implement a `getSupplyAtBlock` endpoint that we could write reference tests for to make sure it is consistent. Obviously the state root would be different if clients had different account balances, but having an easy way to expose it would remove the need to write scripts on top of the clients.

excerpts.author: lastmjs
excerpts.content: Hey everyone, I could really use some help. I'm trying to write a script to verify the total supply of ETH. I'm stuck on the genesis block currently. I know that the initial distribution of ETH is hard-coded somewhere, but I can't seem to find it in the (geth) codebase. The best I've found so far is in this repo: https://github.com/ethereum/pyethsaletool/blob/cab1c9d8ca27f5e86a9eb36a2a56915f5f7830d1/genesis_block.json

excerpts.author: lastmjs
excerpts.content:
That seems to give the correct information for the inintial sale, minus the supply given to the foundation
I really would like to know where this information is stored in geth, and if you have any information about the other clients I would love to know that as well. I really want to be able to trust this initial genesis state, and show to others that it can be trusted.
Thanks!
